Key observations from the test image:
- White cottony/fluffy mycelial growth on the stem
- Black hard sclerotia (dark rounded structures) visible on/in stem tissue
- Brown/bleached stem tissue
- Stem near soil level

This pattern strongly suggests **White Mold** (Sclerotinia stem rot). Let me confirm with reference images.

The White Mold reference perfectly matches — white cottony mycelium on stems with sclerotia. Charcoal Rot shows gray stems with tiny distributed microsclerotia (no fluffy white growth). Let me check a few more candidates.

All other candidates clearly differ:
- **Phytophthora**: wilted plants, brown stem lesions — no white mycelium
- **Rhizoctonia**: reddish-brown stem cankers at soil line — no fluffy growth
- **Pythium_damping_off**: seedling damping off — very young plants collapsing
- **Diaporthe**: tan stem lesions with tiny black pycnidia — no cottony mass

The test image unambiguously shows:
1. **White cottony mycelium** on the stem — the signature sign of *Sclerotinia sclerotiorum*
2. **Large black sclerotia** (hard, irregular structures) embedded in/on the stem — the defining feature of White Mold
3. Bleached/shredded stem tissue consistent with White Mold

The White Mold reference collage is a near-perfect visual match.

The bleached/shredded stem tissue and soil-level location further confirm this. All other stem rot candidates (Charcoal_Rot, Rhizoctonia, Phytophthora, Diaporthe) lack the white fluffy mycelium and large sclerotia entirely."}
